title: Crypto misuse: GCM decrypt inbuf realloc uses exact-fit not doubling — O(n^2) allocations leak timing
description: In wolfssl_aes_gcm_update (wolfssl_aes_gcm.c) decrypt path and kcapi_aead_update, when the inbuf needs to grow, the new allocation is exactly new_len = ctx->inbuf_len + inlen bytes. This means every write() call that grows the buffer triggers a fresh kmalloc + memcpy + memzero_explicit + kfree. For n write() calls of k bytes each, this is O(n^2) work and n kernel allocations. The pattern also creates n-1 heap allocations that contain partial ciphertext and are zeroized then freed. While this is not a cryptographic correctness issue, each old inbuf buffer is correctly zeroized before free, so no plaintext exposure occurs. The timing side-channel is the concern: each additional write() takes progressively longer, potentially revealing the total ciphertext length to a timing-capable observer on the same system. The CBC path already uses a doubling strategy (comparison: wolfssl_aes_cbc uses tail[] fixed-size buffer). The fix is to use a doubling strategy for inbuf growth, same as crypto2dev_fd.c inbuf_append.
